caption: A wedge of cheese sits under the heating element of a raclette grill, and the face nearest the element softens, sags and drips.

sa.check: A wedge of cheese sits under a grill's heating element.
The face nearest the element softens and goes glossy.
The far side of the wedge stays firm.
The softening comes first and the dripping follows.

pc.expect: The softening only advances on the face toward the element and the sag only deepens; the cheese does not stiffen again under the heat.
pc.fail: The sagging face pulls back up into a flat firm face; or a drip retreats into the wedge; or the softened face turns matt and firm again under the element; or the wedge alternates between sagging and firm.

pc.expect: The softened cheese sags downward and drips fall from the wedge's lowest point onto what is below.
pc.fail: The cheese sags upward toward the element; or a drip climbs the wedge; or a drop leaves the wedge and hangs in the air; or melted cheese gathers on the wedge's top face and stays there.

pc.expect: The change is strongest on the face toward the element and least on the side away from it.
pc.fail: The face away from the element sags while the face toward it stays firm; or the whole wedge softens evenly while the element is plainly on one side; or the wedge drips while its surface stays matt and dry.

pc.expect: The softening cheese is a thick liquid that stretches and drips slowly and the rest of the wedge stays a firm solid with a cut edge.
pc.fail: The melted cheese runs as thin as water; or the whole wedge slumps as one soft lump; or the softened face stretches into a strand that snaps back like elastic; or the cheese shatters dry.

pc.expect: One wedge; the cheese goes only from the wedge to what lies below.
pc.fail: The wedge grows; or a second wedge appears; or the wedge vanishes while still whole; or cheese appears on the plate with no drip reaching it.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The grill's frame, the plate and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The grill changes shape; or the plate changes pattern; or items around the grill rearrange.

note: Browning of the cheese's surface is chemistry and is not judged.
